A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLHF–DPO comparison. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: V3 reports original GPT-2 experiments on PKU-SafeRLHF in Section 5 and numerical simulations in Appendices B.8–B.9.

after.justification: V4 retains the original PKU-SafeRLHF experiments and appendix numerical simulations, including their reported outcomes.

M1.justification: V4 adds ℓ0-constrained likelihood estimators, including a shifted variant, alongside the existing ℓ1-regularized estimator in Appendix B.11. These introduce another reward-fitting procedure within the theoretical construction; the implemented RLHF and DPO procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same PKU-SafeRLHF QA, prompt, safer, and better tasks and retain the same three-action numerical simulations. The revised theoretical constructions introduce no new empirically evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Figures 2–5 remain unchanged: RLHF/RL versus DPO variants, reward modeling versus DPO, and the appendix gradient comparisons. The added ℓ0 estimator is analyzed theoretically rather than evaluated as another baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the model sizes, data splits, sample-count sweeps, reward scales, freezing configurations, training budgets, and evaluation procedures. Revised sample-size requirements in Appendix B.11 are theoretical assumptions.

E4.justification: The reward-scale sensitivity study, model-capacity comparisons, sample-efficiency analysis, and appendix numerical cases are retained with the same evidence. No empirical ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report three experimental seeds and retain the same plotted uncertainty. No experimental uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical test changes; the additional probability bounds belong to the theory.

E6.justification: The plotted results in Figures 2–5, numerical examples, and empirical findings are unchanged. V4 reports no additional or corrected empirical performance entries.

T1.justification: Theorems 10–11 and their formal versions add ℓ0 reward-estimation bounds and DPO MLE upper bounds. Assumption 13 replaces tr(Σ_D^-1)=O(d) with eigenvalues of order 1/d, and the DPO lower bounds now explicitly require roughly d² samples up to logarithmic factors. Appendix B.11 adds the shifted ℓ0 proof and replaces the strong-convexity-based policy lower-bound argument with a vocabulary construction and KL inequalities.

C1.justification: The introductory contribution statement now additionally claims a reward-estimation rate of order k log d/n using an ℓ0-constrained estimator, while retaining the earlier square-root rate for ℓ1 regularization. The overarching dichotomy, abstract, and conclusion remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly acknowledges that the estimators are tailored to the task. Appendix B.11 explains the spectral restrictions, and Remark 7 qualifies the policy separation as requiring a specific vocabulary construction rather than relying on a potentially dimension-dependent general-vocabulary bound.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, memory and runtime disclosures, and reported code/data links. Its edits are grammatical rather than changes to reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but v4 expands its use of Yao et al. for sparse estimation and qualifies its relationship to Nika et al. by noting possible dimension dependence in the latter's lower-bound coefficient. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V4 makes local language and notation corrections, updates an author affiliation, and expands explanations around the finite-sample theory. Appendix B.11 gains a proof subsection and receives the existing performance-difference derivation from B.12; the overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: All five figures retain their content and captions. Figures 2–4 shift downward beneath continued experimental discussion, and the expanded theorem displays alter local layout. There is no figure redesign or new table.

improvement.justification: V4 improves the precision and transparency of the finite-sample contribution by revising the Gram-matrix scaling, exposing the lower bounds' sample-size requirements, and distinguishing ℓ0 and ℓ1 guarantees. The gains remain qualified: the faster rate uses the added ℓ0 estimator, and the policy lower bound requires a specialized vocabulary construction. Empirical support is unchanged.
